content:
doc-comments for "panic" and "panic!" contradict to each other.

Function "panic" is defined in Prelude.lean and its doc-comment reads:
===
(panic "msg" : α) has a built-in implementation which prints msg to
the error buffer. It does not terminate execution, and because it is a safe
function, it still has to return an element of α, so it takes [Inhabited α]
and returns default.
===
Macro "panic!" is defined in Lean/Parser/Term.lean and its doc-comment reads:
===
At runtime, msg and the file position are printed to stderr unless the C
function lean_set_panic_messages(false) has been executed before. If the C
function lean_set_exit_on_panic(true) has been executed before, the process is
then aborted.
===
There is clear contradiction here

Docs for function "panic" say that panic does not terminate execution. Words "does not" are emphasized, i. e. it is implied that "panic" definitely always does not terminate execution. But docs for macro "panic!" say that sometimes panic still may terminate the program, if lean_set_exit_on_panic(true) was executed
The right thing here is "panic only terminates execution if the environment variable LEAN_ABORT_ON_PANIC is set or lean_set_exit_on_panic(true) has been run through FFI"
Thank you for answer. Then both doc-comments should be changed
